what: Hand-labelled REVIEW-LADDER set for docs/jev-integration-plan.md 2차 #1 - every failed-prediction peer review dispatched on 2026-09-22 from cycle 75 onwards, with the run that triggered it.
how: archive/peer/2026-09-22-c7*.md and 2026-09-22-c8*.md, excluding priorart / retrospective / outcome files. The trigger log is the FIRST tools/bench/*.log named in the review's `## Question` section; the run inside that log is resolved mechanically as the last BGRUN run that STARTED before the review's `- **date:**` line, because logs are appended to and a reviewed failure is usually no longer the last run (diag_c83_connect2x2_kit.log's reviewed failure is run 0; its last two runs ended rc=0). Labelled by the material session of 2026-09-22 BEFORE any API call, from the review's own question, its outcome line and the triggering run.

classes.our-script-bug: no claim about the machine is in dispute - our own Python died or never reached LabVIEW, or every failing row is a prediction-error (the measured values are right, the expectation was mis-derived). The review was not worth buying.
classes.already-reviewed-class: the same underlying defect had already been asked about in an archived review at the time this one was dispatched, so the ladder should hand the decision to the ordinary discharge.
classes.new-problem: a defect or a blind reader that no archived review covered: the review was worth buying and the gate should block.

note_on_safety: `already-reviewed-class` is NOT by itself an allow. The ladder's branch for it runs the ordinary discharge, which can only cite an exchange that passed guard_peer.review_quality() - so c83-2x2-swap-1055 (outcome TIMEOUT) and c80-rowd-routeA-swapped (outcome TIMEOUT) cannot release anything even though their question text exists on disk. Two of the six already-reviewed labels are exactly that case, on purpose.
